hook.situation: You recommend a drama in KakaoTalk, react to comments, report what a friend said about subtitles, share a video, and troubleshoot a stream that keeps cutting out.
objectives: Ask about watching experience with V(으)ㄴ 적이 있어요.
React naturally to dramas, comments, idols, and shared videos.
Explain streaming problems with 영상이 끊기다 and suggest reconnecting Wi-Fi.
hook.whyItMatters: Entertainment talk in Korean is fast, casual, and full of short reactions. Digital-life Korean also needs practical verbs like 공유하다, 누르다, 끊기다, and 연결하다.

grammarNotes.title: V(으)ㄴ 적이 있어요 — have done it before
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when asking whether someone has the experience of watching, using, or trying content before.
grammarNotes.formation: Add -ㄴ 적이 있어요 after a vowel stem and -은 적이 있어요 after a consonant stem. 보다 becomes 본 적이 있어요. 쓰다 becomes 쓴 적이 있어요. Use 없어요 for no experience.

examples.en: Have you watched this drama before?

examples.ko: 이 배우 나온 영화 본 적 있어요?
examples.romanization: i baeu naon yeonghwa bon jeok isseoyo?
examples.en: Have you watched a movie with this actor before?

examples.ko: 이 앱 써 본 적 있어요?
examples.romanization: i aep sseo bon jeok isseoyo?
examples.en: Have you used this app before?
I have never watched it without subtitles.

exceptions: Use 봤어요 for a dated past event: 어제 봤어요. Use 본 적 있어요 for experience.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-는 것 같아요 — soft opinion or impression
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when you want to recommend or judge content without sounding too absolute.
grammarNotes.formation: Present verbs use -는 것 같아요, adjectives use -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요, and future guesses use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요. In speech, 것 often becomes 거.

examples.en: I think this drama is fun.
It seems like the video keeps cutting out.

examples.ko: 자막이 조금 안 맞는 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: jamagi jogeum an manneun geot gatayo.
examples.en: I think the subtitles are a little off.

examples.ko: 이 아이돌 무대가 대박인 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: i aidol mudaega daebagin geot gatayo.
examples.en: I think this idol's stage is amazing.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-다고 했어요 — said that...
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this to pass along a friend's opinion, recommendation, or warning about content.
grammarNotes.formation: Adjectives take -다고 했어요: 좋다고 했어요, 재미있다고 했어요. Present action verbs take -ㄴ다고/-는다고 했어요. Nouns use (이)라고 했어요.

examples.en: My friend said this drama is fun.
My friend said the subtitles are good.
The comments said the video cuts out often.

examples.ko: 친구가 그 아이돌 무대가 대박이라고 했어요.
examples.romanization: chinguga geu aidol mudaega daebagirago haesseoyo.
examples.en: My friend said that idol's stage was amazing.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-지만 — clean contrast
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when two opinions pull against each other: one good point, one problem, or one comparison.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -지만 directly to the adjective or verb stem. For nouns, use N이지만/지만.

examples.en: The actor is good too, but the comments are more fun.
The drama is fun, but the video cuts out often.
The subtitles are good, but the text is a little small.

examples.ko: 아이돌은 잘 모르지만 이 노래는 좋아요.
examples.romanization: aidoreun jal moreujiman i noraeneun joayo.
examples.en: I do not know idols well, but I like this song.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-거든요 — here's the reason/background
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when you add the reason behind your recommendation or reaction.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -거든요 to the stem: 재미있거든요, 좋거든요, 끊기거든요. It gives background the listener may not know yet.

examples.en: The comments are really fun, you know.
I like this actor, you see.
The video keeps cutting out, you see.
I keep watching because the subtitles are good, you know.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-는데요 — soft setup or problem raising
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this to bring up a problem gently and leave space for the other person to respond.
grammarNotes.formation: Action verbs and 있다/없다 take -는데요. Adjectives take -ㄴ/은데요. In tech support, it often sounds like 'the thing is...'.

examples.en: The video keeps cutting out, though.
The subtitles are not showing, though.
I shared it, but my friend says they couldn't see it.
I did hit like, though.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어 보세요 — try doing it
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this for troubleshooting advice: try reconnecting, try opening again, try checking settings.
grammarNotes.formation: Make the 아/어 form and add 보세요. 연결하다 becomes 연결해 보세요. 누르다 becomes 눌러 보세요.

examples.en: Try reconnecting the Wi-Fi.
Try pressing like.
Try checking the subtitle settings again.
Try sharing the video again.

exampleSentence.en: Have you watched this drama before?
I like this actor, you see.
I think this drama is fun.
The comments are really fun, you know.
My friend said the subtitles are good.
The video keeps cutting out, though.
Did you share the video too?

exampleSentence.en: The video keeps cutting out, though.

They said that idol's stage was amazing.

readingText.title: 영상이 계속 끊기는데요
readingText.body: 민서는 친구에게 새 드라마를 추천했어요. 먼저 '이 드라마 본 적 있어요?'라고 물었어요. 친구는 배우도 좋지만 댓글이 진짜 재미있다고 했어요. 또 자막이 좋아서 한국어 공부에도 도움이 되는 것 같다고 했어요. 민서는 영상을 공유했지만, 친구는 영상이 계속 끊긴다고 했어요. 그래서 민서는 와이파이를 다시 연결해 보라고 했어요. 마지막에는 좋아요도 눌렀는지 물었어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo recommended a new drama to a friend. First, Minseo asked whether the friend had watched it before. The friend said the actor was good, but the comments were really fun. The friend also said the subtitles were good and seemed helpful for Korean study. Minseo shared the video, but the friend said the video kept cutting out. So Minseo told the friend to try reconnecting the Wi-Fi. At the end, Minseo asked whether the friend had also hit like.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 영상이 끊길 때 민서는 무엇을 해 보라고 했어요?

culturalNote.title: Short reactions carry the mood
culturalNote.body: Korean entertainment chats often mix content words with quick reactions. A natural message may be short: 이 드라마 본 적 있어요? 댓글이 진짜 재미있거든요. ㅋㅋ, 헐, and 대박 can make a chat feel natural, but only when they respond to something specific.
culturalNote.tip: Keep digital verbs clear: 댓글을 달다, 좋아요를 누르다, 영상을 공유하다, 와이파이를 연결하다, 영상이 끊기다.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence asks about experience with a drama?
inlineExercises.explanation: -ㄴ 적이 있어요 asks whether someone has done something before.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence reports a friend's opinion?
inlineExercises.explanation: Adjectives use -다고 했어요 in reported speech.
끊기다 describes the video or connection cutting out.

bullets: Core flow: ask if someone has watched a drama, react to comments, report subtitle opinions, share a video, and fix buffering.
Use 본 적 있어요 for experience and -다고 했어요 to report someone else's opinion.
댓글을 달다, 좋아요를 누르다, 영상을 공유하다, and 와이파이를 연결하다 are the key digital action chunks.
영상이 끊기다 describes buffering or cutting out; do not use active 끊다 for that problem.
